sample_unit: complete denture questions (submitted to 7 chatbots, repeated across sessions, in Turkish and English)
models_evaluated: seven AI chatbot systems (others not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Semantic stability of chatbot responses across repeated runs, sessions, and paraphrased prompt variants
links.effect: Model significantly affected semantic stability (p<0.001; ηp2=0.820); stability differed across scheduled query sessions (p<0.001; ηp2=0.055), means 0.863, 0.874, 0.841 for morning, afternoon, evening.
links.quote: semantic stability differed across scheduled query sessions (p < 0.001; ηp2 = 0.055), with means of 0.863 ± 0.106, 0.874 ± 0.092, and 0.841 ± 0.140 for morning, afternoon, and evening sessions, respectively.

links.outcome: Consistency of chatbot responses across semantically equivalent prompt variants and repeated queries
links.effect: AI model significantly affected embedding-based semantic stability (p<0.001; ηp2=0.820); Grok highest overall stability mean (0.952 ± 0.015); English showed higher similarity than Turkish conditions overall (p<0.001).
links.quote: English responses showed higher overall GQS than the original Turkish responses (3.96 ± 0.94 vs. 3.66 ± 1.23; p = 0.004) and higher embedding-based similarity than the Turkish conditions overall (p < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the quality and semantic stability of responses from seven AI chatbots to complete denture questions in Turkish and English without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
